Phonemes in major syllables': 'Most Kammu words consist of one major syllable, or a major syllabe preceded by a minor syllabe. Major syllables have the structure C(C)V(C). The minor syllables will be described later…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables: one major (main) syllable, optionally preceded by one minor syllable. The minor syllable is short and unstressed; prominence therefore falls on the major syllable, which is the last syllable of the word. The minor-syllable system, and by implication this stress pattern, is stated to be essentially the same in all Kammu dialects including Khween.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. The northern dialects, Khween among them, have a lexical high/low tone contrast in some words (p.46-49), so the language is marginally tonal as well; in Yuan, Khween and Uu the syllabic-nasal minor syllables begin with a toneless phase and a more or less articulated vowel (p.49).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (major syllable plus optional minor syllable), based on ~550-item Egerod-based word-lists in citation form; Khween data come from word-lists recorded with two speakers (p.45). The statement is made for Kammu dialects jointly, not for Khween alone.
new_statements.identity_note: Khuen [khf] has no dedicated description. Glottolog 5.3 states it is 'not appreciably different from the Yuan dialect of Khmu' (Svantesson p.c. 2011; the only difference being Buddhism, Izikowitz 1951:24), and the SEAlang MK classification lists 'Khmu Khwen / Khuen / Khween' as a Khmu dialect under kjg+khf. The quoted source (Lindell, Svantesson & Tayanin 1981) treats Khween as one Kammu tmooy (dialect group) beside Yuan, Rook, Kroong, Lii and Uu, with Khween data from word-lists of two speakers, and makes its minor-syllable/stress statement for all Kammu dialects jointly. So the statement is first-hand for Khween as a named variety but is a Khmu-wide description; the catalog already holds Khmu (khmu1256) via Suwilai 1987 with the same final-major-syllable pattern. If Khuen is kept as a separate catalog row, it should be marked as covered by a Kammu dialect survey that includes Khween rather than a Khuen-specific grammar; the closest-named variety is Khmu Yuan (khmu1256, Northern Kammu).
